name: Juche
summary: Juche is the state ideology of North Korea: a self-reliance doctrine that began as a variant of Marxism-Leninism and holds that the masses are masters of their destiny but need the party and a supreme leader (suryong) to guide them. It demands political independence, an autarkic planned economy built on heavy industry, and military self-reliance, and it opposes dependence on great powers and imperialism. In its developed Kimilsungist-Kimjongilist form it adds a hereditary leader cult, one-party rule, collectivist duties over individual rights, and military-first (Songun) policy.
scope: The state doctrine of the DPRK as codified by Kim Il Sung's 1955 and 1967 speeches and Kim Jong Il's 1982 treatise On the Juche Idea, the Ten Principles of 1974 and the DPRK constitution, as it stood in the Kim Jong Il era (Songun included). It excludes the South Korean student Jusapa faction and foreign Juche study groups, and later Kim Jong Un-era revisions (people-first politics, 2024-26 constitutional changes) are noted but not the basis. Where sources say nothing, answers are inferred from these principles.

keyFigures.name: Kim Il Sung
keyFigures.role: Founder of North Korea, credited with originating Juche and the 1955 Juche speech.

keyFigures.name: Kim Jong Il
keyFigures.role: Declared Juche a distinct ideology and authored On the Juche Idea (1982).

keyFigures.name: Hwang Jang-yop
keyFigures.role: Philosopher credited by Western scholars with Juche's early development.

sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Ownership, planned economy, party and army roles, citizen duties, religion, women, foreign policy and the nuclear programme.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The state owns the means of production and claims responsibility for citizens' welfare, so free state-guaranteed health care fits the socialist system the constitution describes.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set by the state plan, so the question hardly arises; inferred that adherents favour higher pay set by the state rather than opposing it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The treatise demands an independent national economy built on planning and self-reliance, and the constitution commits to a planned economy rather than market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Constitution Articles 20-23 make the main means of production state and cooperative property, so utilities and heavy industry are publicly owned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The system has no large private wealth by design; inferred that adherents would accept heavy taxation of wealth, though the constitution emphasises state ownership rather than taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Unions exist only as party-led transmission belts, so adherents would value organised labour but not independent unions; the issue is truly split between the two readings.

property-fundamental.rationale: Economic resources are state and collective property; the constitution permits only limited personal property, so private property is not a fundamental inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Private corporations are marginal in the planned economy; inferred that tight state control of any firm is accepted, though the question is not directly addressed.

cut-welfare.rationale: The state presents itself as provider of free education, housing and care; the constitution's collectivist principle of one for all would reject cutting welfare as harmful dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is vested in the state and cooperatives under party leadership, not in workers' own enterprises, so autonomous worker ownership is not the model.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Citizens are required by the constitution to remain vigilant for state security, and the party-state relies on pervasive monitoring.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Citizens must observe socialist living standards and work discipline under the constitution; drug legalisation would be rejected as a decadent bourgeois practice.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech is controlled by the party-state, but the focus is on loyalty rather than hate speech as such; inferred mild agreement with legal limits on speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The suryong theory holds that the leader is the centre of the masses and an absolute supreme leader, and the treatise calls on all to rally around the party and leader.

state-harmful.rationale: The treatise says independence is expressed through state power and the working class must become master of it; Juche is a state-building ideology and rejects anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed force is monopolised by the party-led army and the all-people defence system; inferred that civilian ownership is unneeded, though the militarised population is armed through the reserve forces.

empower-police-military.rationale: Songun made the military the first priority of state, and the army's mission is defending the party and system under Articles 59-60.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socialist living standards are an explicit citizen duty, and the state treats sex work as a bourgeois vice; inferred from that duty.

decide-locally.rationale: Democratic centralism (Article 5) subordinates lower bodies to the centre, and the leader-centred unity doctrine rejects local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Official doctrine speaks of re-educating wrongdoers, but practice is harsh and punitive; the position is split between rhetoric and practice.

traditional-family.rationale: Scholars such as Armstrong describe Juche as familism with the leader as father, and traditional family forms are promoted, while the state also mobilises women into work.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Official socialist moral standards and familist ideology give no room for recognising same-sex marriage; inferred from the socialist living standards duty.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion is legal and not discussed as a moral issue in the constitution, while the state is also pronatalist; adherents lean modestly toward legal access.

more-religion-public.rationale: The constitution guarantees belief nominally but Juche functions as a quasi-religion that tolerates no rival public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Juche focuses on national independence and Korean unity, not domestic racial injustice; the issue is essentially absent and not inferable.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Article 77 asserts women's equality with men as a socialist principle, which implies roles are not innate, though official gender norms remain traditional.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The treatise says culture should be national in form and socialist in content and stresses knowing Korean history and customs, with national dignity and pride.

gradual-change.rationale: The treatise stresses that a revolution begins with struggle and old forces never yield voluntarily, though the established North Korean order itself is to be defended.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Juche emphasises the Korean nation and national sovereignty and the state is closed to immigration; inferred from nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The treatise makes independence from outside direction the life and soul of a sovereign state, so empowering international bodies over states is rejected.

free-trade.rationale: The treatise warns that economic dependence undermines independence and calls for a self-sufficient national economy rather than open trade.

nation-first.rationale: National independence and self-reliance come first; the treatise nonetheless allows cooperation with socialist and newly emerging countries.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Article 17 rests foreign relations on independence while Juche denounces interference in other nations' affairs as dominationism.

open-borders.rationale: The ideology's stress on the nation-state, sovereignty and Korean identity is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The treatise treats economic development of heavy industry and technology as the material basis of independence.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Neither source discusses climate; Juche supports technical progress and heavy industry, but state-directed action would be easy for it to endorse.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The treatise pairs a technical revolution with a cultural one, but holds that people's ideology and consciousness, not technology alone, decide outcomes.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The nuclear programme is written into the constitution as a deterrent, and self-sufficiency in energy and arms is a Juche goal.

revolution-justified.rationale: The treatise states that a revolution begins with struggle and that old ruling forces never give up power voluntarily, treating revolution as a necessity of history.

experts-over-public.rationale: The treatise sees the masses as masters of revolution and construction but needing leadership; expertise serves the party line rather than governing over the public.

central-planning.rationale: The treatise calls for an independent national economy built on state direction and the constitution (Articles 19, 26, 34) commits to a planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: The constitution allows cost, price and profit accounting (Article 33) under planning and some cooperative property, but markets as an organising principle are not endorsed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land belongs to the state or cooperatives, so a land-value tax replacing other taxes is not part of the model; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Article 24 protects personal property including inheritance, yet there is no substantial private wealth to tax; the issue is not addressed.

basic-income.rationale: Work discipline is a citizen duty and the treatise stresses labour; inferred that unconditional income without work is not favoured.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The treatise's autarkic economic line, with state trade monopolies, aims to protect and build domestic industry from foreign dependence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The treatise wants an independent national economy built on heavy industry and the constitution has the state budget follow the economic plan (Article 35).

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is state and cooperative, not spread among small owners, though personal and small-scale property are tolerated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The treatise says material incentives are not ignored under socialism and the constitution keeps cost, price and profit accounting; abolition is a distant communist goal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The state controls the whole economy and budget, so abolishing central banking to leave money to the market contradicts the system.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Labour and management are both under party-state direction, not bargaining bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Workers' Party is the sole guiding force of the state and Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism the guiding ideology, with the army sworn to defend the party Central Committee.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Juche formally rejects monarchy but the hereditary leadership succession is defended; adherents are genuinely ambiguous.

democracy-best.rationale: Juche claims the masses are masters and the constitution provides elections, but it rejects liberal multi-party democracy where voters might choose against the leader line.

direct-votes.rationale: Official elections are uncontested and policy flows from the party leadership; direct referendums are not a feature.

workers-councils.rationale: Power rests with the party and democratic centralism (Article 5), not with autonomous councils replacing the state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Juche stresses national sovereignty and unity; secession would be seen as weakening the unified nation.

natural-rulers.rationale: The suryong theory holds the leader is a uniquely supreme figure and leadership has been hereditary within the Kim family.

political-violence-never.rationale: The treatise holds revolution begins and ends with struggle and old ruling forces must be forced from power.

war-builds-character.rationale: Songun glorifies the army, but doctrine frames defence as necessity rather than ennobling war; adherents are split on the claim as worded.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 68 guarantees belief but the state ideology is quasi-religious; nominal separation exists alongside state veneration, so the answer is split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law derives from the party's ideology and the constitution, not religious scripture, and Juche is nominally secular.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts and defence belong to the state; the army and all-people defence system are state organs under Articles 58-60.

military-superiority.rationale: The treatise says self-reliance in defence is a fundamental principle and the state maintains a very large army and nuclear missiles.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Critics such as Myers describe Juche as ultranationalist, and Armstrong calls it nationalist in content, centred on the Korean nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The treatise puts the masses' consciousness and creativity as the driving force of history and keeps class struggle, but gives the leading role to ideology rather than class conflict alone.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The system claims egalitarian socialist distribution but with a rank-based privileged class; the claimed doctrine leans to equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous claims are not a Juche theme; the unitary nation-state model implies sovereignty rests with the central state.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Juche is rooted in anti-imperialism and opposes dominationism, so reparations from former colonial powers fit its stance (inferred).

civilizational-union.rationale: Juche emphasises the independent nation-state and national sovereignty above civilizational blocs, though it cooperates with non-aligned and socialist states.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Article 63 states the principle of one for all and all for one and the treatise criticises capitalism's profit orientation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Articles 81-86 list citizens' duties of political unity, discipline and defence, and rights and duties rest on the collective principle.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The treatise puts humans as masters of everything and nature as something to be transformed; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: The state has been pronatalist and values population as national strength and labour; inferred from that stance.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The treatise treats industrialisation and technical revolution as the foundation of independence and socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The treatise calls for a technical revolution, but it is to be directed by the party and not allowed to disrupt the leader-led order.

human-enhancement.rationale: Individual bodily autonomy is subordinate to collective aims; inferred and not addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The treatise holds that people's consciousness and the leader's guidance decide; machines taking governance over is not a Juche theme.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Citizens must be vigilant for state security and the state tightly controls information; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Juche presents itself as revolutionary and forward-building toward communism, but it also stresses national tradition; the balance favours progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The treatise says ideology defines human worth and quality and holds that correct ideology guides action, so ideology beats pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: The treatise values mass mobilisation but organised under the party and the state; direct action against institutions is not endorsed once in power.

means-match-ends.rationale: Juche supports disciplined hierarchical revolutionary means to build a communist society; the prefigurative claim is not endorsed.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The treatise values technical and economic development and the cultural revolution; a return to foraging is the opposite.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The treatise lists building communism as a long-term goal but works with the worker-peasant alliance and specialised planning; abolition is not an aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution by need is the ultimate declared goal, with socialist distribution by work in the meantime.

production-for-use.rationale: The treatise contrasts socialism with capitalism's profit orientation, though the constitution keeps profit accounting within planning.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The treatise criticises capitalism and imperialism as exploitative, though Juche's own stress is on independence more than labour theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Juche originated in Marxism-Leninism and holds that the working class must master state power, though the 1992 constitution dropped the phrase.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural land is cooperative or state property, and cooperative farms are a constitutional form of ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The treatise names imperialism as the main enemy of national independence, implying its link to domination and war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Citizens are required to protect state property and work for the collective; the principle of taxation-as-theft is rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Citizens' duties include observing socialist living standards, so the state may restrict conduct beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article 63 gives the collectivist principle and rights are tied to duties to the collective.

conscription.rationale: Article 86 makes military service a citizen's duty and the state maintains a universal conscript system.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The state restricts emigration and demands loyalty; both exit and electoral voice are subordinate to unity.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a socialist party-led collective, not a firm serving customers who can exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Constitution guarantees material provisions such as work, education and care as socialist rights, which adherents would present as the substance of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and academia are controlled by the party and have no independent power; the question assumes a liberal system.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Critics describe Juche as ultranationalist; ability differences between races are not discussed directly, so inference only.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through party-led mass organisations and the SPA, a corporatist-looking structure but not the family-based model described.

total-state.rationale: The party-state directs economy, culture and education under the monolithic ideological system, and the Ten Principles govern political and social life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Survival and revival of the nation are guiding principles, particularly after the Eastern Bloc collapse, but the framing of decadence is not used.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The state aims to reunify Korea on its terms but not expand as an empire; the 2026 constitution dropped reunification, so the position is unsettled.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to the leader is central but is framed as party-ideological loyalty, not feudal oaths of lords; split.

bound-labor.rationale: Cooperative farmers are members of cooperatives, and the system rejects feudal bondage; collectivism is not the same as bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The treatise holds that ideology shapes people's thought and that knowledge serves class and national interest; neutral knowledge is not asserted.

universal-morality.rationale: The treatise stresses that morality has class and national character and puts the masses' independence as the measure.

single-common-good.rationale: The leader as centre of the masses and the doctrine of unified purpose imply one common good, set by the party line.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Article 17 supports foreign liberation struggles and North Korea has opposed Israel, but the issue is not addressed directly.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Juche is concerned with Korean nation and diaspora in Japan and elsewhere, but right of return is not documented; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Korean is the language of the state and not a lapsed one, so the question is hypothetical; inferred sympathy only.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic centralism and the masses-as-masters theory give formal worker participation, while management is under party direction.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is state-provided universal and free under the socialist system, with no private choice schemes.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The state budget follows the economic plan, and deficit concerns are not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The treatise grounds freedom in independence and collectivism rather than in market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The leader theory presents the leader as moral parent and exemplar, though the state relies heavily on law and coercion too.

national-self-determination.rationale: The treatise states political independence is the life and soul of a sovereign state and nations have a right to self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Juche rejects deference to great powers and the UN; use of force abroad is not an active doctrine, so inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Scholars describe Juche as quasi-religious with a sacred leader, though it claims scientific materialist roots.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits are tied to citizens in a closed state; the issue of immigrants does not arise.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work discipline is a constitutional duty and labour is the basis of socialist distribution.

class-collaboration.rationale: The treatise keeps class struggle and class consciousness, though in the state's own framing class antagonisms have been resolved internally.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Culture is to be national in form and socialist in content, so inherited culture is reshaped rather than discarded.

dominated-front.rationale: North Korea joined the Non-Aligned Movement and promotes Juche as an anti-imperialist model for developing countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Juche subordinates internationalism to national independence and nation-state sovereignty, with cooperation among socialist states.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 77 gives women equal status, but official practice and familist ideology keep distinct roles; split.

ban-interest.rationale: The state banking system uses interest and price accounting under Article 33; no ban is documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Juche is racialised in its nationalism but legal segregation within the state is not part of the doctrine.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The treatise says the working class must become master of state power and the state serves class ends; the Marxist-Leninist view of the state is inherited.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Self-sufficiency in energy and resources, using domestic coal, is a stated economic pillar.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not a Juche issue given closed borders; the ethnic nationalist outlook implies assimilation if any.

elite-replacement.rationale: This is a Western far-right conspiracy theory not part of Juche; inferred rejection.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections are single-list for the SPA, and multi-party proportional contests are not part of the system.

national-mission.rationale: North Korea promotes Juche abroad through international seminars and institutes as a model for the Third World.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The constitution declares women equal and the official line holds that socialism has ended women's subordination.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party-state presents the leadership as embodying the masses' interests; criticism of the elite is not permitted.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a documented Juche theme; the state is pronatalist, so inferred disagreement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The army and security organs are defended as guardians of the party and system and answer to the leadership.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state directs the economy and ideology, which is the opposite of a limited state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Critics such as Myers read Juche as ultranationalist and ethnically centred on the Korean nation, which implies discouraging mixing; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution declares equal rights and the treatise holds that all people are masters, but the system ranks citizens by loyalty class.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Juche developed as a defence of building socialism in one country with national self-reliance, and its 'socialism of our style' rejected mechanical imitation of the Soviet experience.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The statement concerns cases such as Israel or Americas; Juche opposes imperialism but the claim is not addressed directly.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One legal system applies to all citizens and religion has no civil legal role.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 68 guarantees belief nominally but state ideology discourages religious influence; unknown.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No religious basis exists for such a ban and state collectives raise cattle for food.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: State education is ideological and secular, teaching Juche and leader biographies, not religion.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Juche presents the state as needing to be strengthened for survival against hostile encirclement, a principle emphasised especially after the Eastern Bloc collapse.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The ideology claims the masses as masters and elections confirm the leader, but legitimacy rests on the leader's role; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Autarkic economics prioritises self-reliance; export surplus is not a stated aim but import reduction is.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a documented Juche principle; inferred disagreement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The treatise accepts revolutionary force and the army's role, so a strict non-aggression principle is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The treatise grounds progress in the creative cooperation of the unified masses and not competition between individuals.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Only the Workers' Party and its allied parties are permitted and opposition is not tolerated.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The treatise defines independence as freedom from domination by outside powers, a national analogue; applied to individuals it is not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 5 sets democratic centralism with all organs under the party and the SPA, not checks between separate bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The treatise calls the party the general staff of the revolution that the masses need for correct leadership.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialist ideals favour the poor and the state claims universal provision, though the doctrine puts the nation first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing is state-allocated and ownership is limited; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Independent strikes are not permitted and work discipline is a constitutional duty.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The treatise attributes poverty to dependence and exploitation rather than to population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The ethnic nationalism holds the homogeneous Korean nation as a strength; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are filled by party appointment and slated elections, not by lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Ten Principles and party charter supersede the constitution in practice and state security demands vigilance; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices are set by the state under the plan, so fixed prices on essentials are standard.

party-controls-media.rationale: All media is controlled by the ruling party and state under the monolithic ideological system.

party-commands-army.rationale: Article 59 assigns the armed forces to defend the Workers' Party Central Committee, and the party commands the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not an operative question in a closed state; no position is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian socialist principles favour modest pay for officials, though privileges for the elite are known; split toward agreement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism (Article 5) and the Ten Principles require members and organs to carry out decisions of the higher party leadership.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The treatise names political independence as the life and soul of a sovereign state, so pooling sovereignty in a supranational union is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The supreme leader commands all armed forces and is head of the state's defence organs, while legislature has little role.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religion is not a state matter and has no national church; inferred disagreement from secular ideology.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rests in the party and leader, not religious scholars, and Juche is a secular state ideology.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Juche stresses national defence and unity behind the leader; working people defeating their own government in war is the opposite.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The treatise holds that culture must be socialist in content and the state directs art toward ideological education.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The leader's tenure is lifelong and the position is not subject to term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Representatives are formally accountable to voters under Articles 6-7, but removal is at the party's direction; split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Juche opposes dependence on great powers and flunkeyism, but allows allied military aid if the state is strong on its own, so agreement is moderate.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is state-allocated rather than family owned; this model is not a Juche theme.

people-in-arms.rationale: Article 58 establishes an all-people defence system, with the armed forces drawn from the working people, but a professional army remains central.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture is valued as part of the worker-peasant alliance, yet the model prizes heavy industry; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification under independence and peace was the long-held constitutional goal (Article 9, formerly), though the 2024-26 revisions turned against it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The treatise values intellectuals and aims to intellectualise society, but sees the revolutionary intelligentsia remoulded by working-class stance; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The treatise stresses equality among nations and each nation's right to its own national form of culture.

death-penalty.rationale: The state applies capital punishment to severe crimes including offences against the state.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Socialist moral standards and familist ideology suggest limited sex education; gender equality is supported but the combined claim is split toward disagreement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Juche claims a scientific materialist basis and treats religion as incompatible with its own doctrine.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Citizens must observe socialist living standards and the state bans pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Korean nation is conceived as a blood-related community and citizenship passes by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The unitary Korean nation is the stress and minority issues are barely acknowledged; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Duties to the state, including military service under Article 86, come before individual claims.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to the monolithic ideological system and socialist living standards is demanded, and eccentric individualism is condemned.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The treatise opposes domination of poor nations by outside powers; inferred sympathy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The treatise says political independence rests on economic self-sufficiency and that an independent national economy is the material basis of independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional amendment requires two-thirds of the SPA under Article 97 and the party leads; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The state has justified discipline and sacrifice for economic construction under the party's guidance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Juche prizes self-reliance over aid yet backs solidarity among developing nations; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The 2023 amendment wrote the nuclear programme into the constitution as a deterrent against the United States, and Juche demands military self-reliance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The leader's position is set by party succession and not by popular election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The central bank is a state organ under the planned economy and budget.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Juche's unification claim treats the whole peninsula as the national territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is held mainly by the state and cooperatives for the collective, and personal property is protected only in limited form.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Juche criticised Soviet de-Stalinisation and revisionism but did not call the USSR state-capitalist; Kim Jong Il said Eastern Bloc socialism failed by mechanical imitation.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and neither supported nor opposed in doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: The treatise accepts allied military aid if the state is strong on its own; collective defence pacts are tolerated, not central.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Juche's anti-imperialism and nationalism would treat unconsented annexation as occupation, as with its view of the US presence in South Korea.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious bodies are controlled by the party-state, which allows only supervised organisations.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The leader is head of the party and the state, so a nonpartisan figurehead contradicts the system.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity and sovereignty are central, so force to keep the state intact follows.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The state's reunification formulas have included a federation keeping two systems, though now abandoned; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Scholars compare Juche to Korean religions and State Shinto with a sacred leader, and the Kim family leaders are venerated.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The state does not run a progressive personal income tax; inferred disagreement on grounds of its planned economy.

character-from-environment.rationale: The treatise says people can be remoulded by ideology and education and that thoughts define human worth, so environment matters most.

space-expansion.rationale: The state sees space programmes as proof of scientific self-reliance; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Ten Principles and party charter supersede the constitution in practice and the leader has absolute authority.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The state concentrates power in the party and leader rather than mixing powers between classes.

leader-cult.rationale: The suryong theory casts the leader as the centre of the masses and the Ten Principles require loyalty, with portraits and mass praise a central practice.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The treatise says revolution begins and ends with struggle and calls for continued vigilance; the idea that party leaders may restore capitalism is a Maoist notion not stressed, so agreement is moderate.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform of 1946 and collectivisation underlie the system; the statement's present-tense scope is moderate.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Juche treats Korea as one nation, but claims beyond the peninsula are not documented.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious freedom is nominal in the constitution while Juche discourages rival faiths; not a documented legal norm.

women-must-cover.rationale: Article 77 gives women equal status and the doctrine has no basis for compulsory covering.

common-currency.rationale: The independent national economy implies separate national currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Juche focuses on the Korean nation; a pan-ethnic union is not a theme.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minorities are barely acknowledged and unity is stressed; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not a Juche theme; the doctrine addresses Korean diaspora but not this debate.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Juche departs from Marxism by putting people's consciousness and ideology as the driving force of history rather than material conditions alone.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state economy is monopolised by the state; competition law is irrelevant.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state owns and supports state enterprises; inferred disagreement.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Courts are party-directed; the statement refers to liberal constitutions and does not apply.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women have formal equal rights, but quotas are not documented in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The treatise stresses self-sufficiency and warns against dependence on outside powers, though it rejects isolation and does not need colonies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Juche favours state control of trade rather than binding international standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: The treatise says political and moral incentives should come first under socialism, with material incentives not ignored.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kim Il Sung's guerrilla background underlies the ideology's military-first character, though the party-led reading is central.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The suryong succession within the Kim family is hereditary, so hereditary privileges are not rejected in principle.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The treatise stresses that Koreans should know their own history and national dignity, with history centred on the nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The treatise condemns dominationism and holds that nations are equal with a right to self-determination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Schools teach loyalty to the leader and nation and the treatise stresses national dignity and pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; not a Juche issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state controls the monetary system as part of the planned economy; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The treatise portrays capitalism and imperialism as in decline and Juche as the way forward.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Juche opposes domination by great powers, so cultivating influence over former subjects would be seen as dominationism.

delink-world-market.rationale: The treatise stresses self-reliance but says economic self-reliance does not mean isolation and encourages cooperation with newly emerging nations; split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no position inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The doctrine does not admit private owners' freedom to refuse service; the state organises all economic life.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights come with duties under Article 63 and the Ten Principles supersede the constitution in practice.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Juche arose in resistance to Japanese rule and opposes imperial domination; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The leadership passed hereditarily within the Kim family, so election of rulers is not the model.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism subordinates the minority to the majority and the higher organs.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Loyalty to the leader is absolute under the Ten Principles, so resisting him is rejected.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The party and leader hold ultimate authority and the SPA is formal, though the constitution calls it the highest organ.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The treatise places humans as masters of everything; animal welfare is not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no position inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Obligation to the less fortunate is a collective, state matter rather than a duty of a privileged class.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Citizens are obliged to take part in organisational life and political work; withdrawal is condemned.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed directly; Juche sees culture as a tool of the revolution, not as pacifying.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the Gramscian theory is not part of Juche.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The treatise names imperialism as the main enemy of independence, implying that the world economy disadvantages poor nations.

native-born-offices.rationale: The ethnically centred nation-state and the loyalty class system imply this; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: After the 1956 August Faction Incident the state purged pro-Soviet and pro-Chinese elements and stayed neutral in the Sino-Soviet split, insisting on its own road without outside interference.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The treatise makes self-reliance a fundamental principle, calling on a nation to rely on its own initiative and resources rather than on others.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not a Juche issue; the unitary nation-state does not differentiate.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: North Korea's founding legitimacy is anchored in anti-Japanese struggle, but constitutional doctrine on democracy is not the model.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Juche presents itself as socialist and anti-imperialist and critics who compare it to fascism are rejected by the state.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: State monuments honouring the leaders are central to the cult, so preservation of honoured figures is favoured.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Juche rejects mechanical imitation of foreign experience, and Kim Jong Il held that Eastern Bloc socialism failed by imitating the Soviet model; each nation needs its own forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Songun and Article 59 make the army defender of party and system with a leading political role.

filial-duty.rationale: Armstrong's familism reading puts parent-child loyalty at the centre, with the leader as father.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posts go by party selection and loyalty rather than competitive examination; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The state controls foreign trade and investment through state institutions and independence demands protection of strategic sectors.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Elected bodies answer to the party hierarchy and not to binding mandates from voters.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions are provided by the state; private accounts contradict collective provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land belongs to the state and cooperatives, with individuals holding use rights only.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The SPA approves the budget formally under the constitution, but without independent power.

single-official-language.rationale: The unitary Korean nation uses Korean in state and schooling.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land belongs to the state and cooperatives, so foreign ownership is excluded.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The treatise stresses ideological remoulding and moral incentives over material pursuits.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Article 17 commits the state to support foreign liberation struggles; arming hostile governments' insurgents is a stronger claim.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Juche opposes great-power interference and resisted Soviet and Chinese meddling.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The state controls information and foreign contact tightly.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The state favours population growth for the nation and promotes births; inferred from the national stance.

residents-only-property.rationale: Residence is state-controlled and property allocation is local; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The constitution frames work as a right and duty and the state assigns jobs.

democratic-peace.rationale: The treatise holds that imperialism rather than regime type drives war; spreading democracy is seen as domination.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Citizens must observe the laws under the constitution, and obedience to the leader's line is required.

non-intervention.rationale: The treatise names dominationism and interference as enemies of national independence and holds that nations are equal.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions are party-led mass organisations; the craft-versus-industry question is not addressed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not a documented theme, though the state blames external enemies.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Familism and the traditional family are central, so abolishing legal marriage is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The state controls information and restricts access.

local-production.rationale: The treatise stresses national self-sufficiency, not local; split.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party is a disciplined vanguard organisation; informal groups are rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Political independence and sovereignty are placed above outside direction.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by blood and Juche, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The treatise condemns flunkeyism toward great powers as especially harmful and rejects dependence on them.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 24 protects personal property while means of production are state or cooperative.

defeat-communism.rationale: Juche presents itself as a socialist and communist-building ideology and opposes anti-communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Services are provided by the state; mixed provision contradicts state ownership.

religion-illusion.rationale: Juche is nominally secular and materialist in origin but functions as a quasi-religion; mild agreement.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist-Leninist roots recognise capitalism's historical role, but the treatise stresses it as exploitative and imperialist.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Article 77 and socialist doctrine tie women's equality to the socialist system; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The state mobilises women into work, but the familist ideology places care in the family; split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cultural nationalism and national form in culture suggest favouring linguistic purity; the sources do not discuss language policy, so inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The state and party direct a centralised system, not small autonomous communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Juche claims to be a socialist path and rejects third-way framings, though it declares its own style of socialism.

corporate-influence.rationale: Private corporations play no role in the planned state economy, so the claim does not arise; inferred neutral.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist strain in the sources and the state's claim to the whole peninsula, with Mount Paektu as sacred origin.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-fascist state tradition, though Juche rarely engages the question.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not in the treatise; inferred from the collectivist moral order and the state's conservative line on sexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The constitution gives the party leadership of all state activity and Juche forbids dissent from the leader.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the state treats the leader cult as quasi-religious and restricts other religion, though the constitution nominally protects belief.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The treatise makes opposition to imperialism and colonial dependence central to independence.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Juche backs resistance to invasion but frames it as a national duty, not a religious one; no firm position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Juche rejects religious law as a standard of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Juche says the masses are masters of their destiny but also that they need the party and leader to guide them, so it is split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: the treatise frames oppression as national and class struggle and does not use this analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the state's conservative social order.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the collectivist view that life belongs to the socio-political body of the nation.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed; Juche presents itself as its own system rather than a blend, but claims to transcend narrow class doctrine.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the treatise criticises capitalist exploitation, though it does not use the alienation concept.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns national independence, with no view on Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the masses led by the suryong, and Juche claims to replace religion with its own doctrine.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the state's secular and anti-religious posture in public institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the state economy makes the question hardly arise.

social-market-economy.rationale: The constitution sets a state-owned planned economy, not a market economy with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Self-reliant defence is a pillar of Juche and Songun puts the army first.

rich-first.rationale: The economy is state-planned with collective ownership, leaving no room for letting some prosper first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Independence and refusal of dependence on great powers are core to Juche, and the constitution states an independent foreign policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Developed Juche in the Kim Jong Il era has a hereditary leader: the suryong theory and the party and leader cult passed from Kim Il Sung to Kim Jong Il.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The constitution sets state and cooperative ownership and a planned economy, leaving no room for user-owned or independent banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Self-reliance and political independence are the core of the doctrine, and the treatise opposes dependence on great powers and imperialism.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution gives nominally universal suffrage to citizens, and the doctrine is built on the masses as masters; wealth qualifications run against its form.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The treatise has man as master of the world who transforms nature, so nature is to be mastered rather than spared; the link to women's domination is not made.

reification.rationale: Juche began within Marxism-Leninism but dropped materialism for the human-centred idea; the concept of reification is not addressed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: private ownership is excluded and the state runs all media, and the doctrine treats bourgeois freedoms as class-based.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1974 Ten Principles and the leader theory place the supreme leader's instruction above ordinary rules, so rule by case-by-case directive is the norm.

racial-franchise.rationale: Juche stresses Korean national unity, but the constitution grants the vote to citizens and does not create an ethnic franchise; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from party and leader control of information and collective duties over individual rights; the doctrine predates the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the party and leader's guiding role and state control of information.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religion is formally free but marginal under Juche, which functions as a quasi-religion; legal bars on mixed marriage are inferred as unlikely.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the state owns commerce and enforces collective unity, and the constitution protects religious belief nominally.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the party guides the masses, and decisions come from the party and leader, not from randomly chosen citizens.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Juche treats itself as the guiding idea and religion as marginal, so reform of religious doctrine is outside its concerns.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: State ownership and planned economy under the constitution limit private wealth, though the doctrine does not discuss liberty and wealth; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist, military-first culture; the opened sources do not discuss gay military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Juche idea works as the state ideology taught in schools, displacing religion in practice, though the constitution formally allows religion; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Juche holds that the masses need party and leader guidance and defends the dictatorship of the proletariat, so police and prisons are kept as instruments of the state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Juche requires a single supreme leader (suryong) and one-party rule, so power is not shared among communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The constitution makes the state responsible for citizens' welfare in a planned economy, so charity-over-state-aid contradicts it.

term-limits.rationale: Juche's developed form includes a hereditary supreme leader with no tenure limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: The leader-guided masses doctrine and one-party rule rule out individual vote delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by Juche texts; an inferred neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is outside the doctrine; the sources do not address it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution declares women equal to men in social life, so shared marital authority fits; inferred, since the Confucian family order persists in practice.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the one-party constitution and the limited political rights; participation is reserved for citizens, and foreigners are excluded.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of the means of production and state housing; rent control is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the state-owned economy; intellectual property is not addressed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The state runs mass youth organisations, such as the Korean Children's Union and the Socialist Patriotic Youth League, and Songun stresses military training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: North Korea has its own nuclear programme, which the constitution names, and would not exclude nuclear weapons from its territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Independence and anti-imperialism are central to Juche; the treatise demands political and military independence from great powers.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Juche's anti-imperialism accuses the United States of massacres in the Korean War; formal recognition is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The constitution states the socialist principle of distribution according to the quantity and quality of work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Songun military-first politics and the collectivist duty to defend the leader and country imply no pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Juche's nationalism treats the Korean nation as a unified ethnic whole with a continuous history from antiquity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist views on gender in the regime's collectivist ideology; the sources do not discuss it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's treatment of women as a group with defined state roles; not discussed directly.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The leader cult honours the revolutionary dead, and the state maintains martyrs' cemeteries.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Juche is atheist, but it acts as a quasi-religion; a good-versus-evil spiritual framing is not stated.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from reunification of the Korean nation under a single state, which seeks to gather rather than diffuse.

culture-before-state.rationale: Kim Jong Il's treatise puts the party and state as the leading force; cultural renewal follows political independence.

god-not-male.rationale: Juche is atheist and does not address the gender of God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the treatise's materialism, which rejects religion as a standard of judgement.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Juche's ethnic nationalism and homogeneity, which favours the Korean majority; the sources do not discuss minorities.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the demand for reunification of Korea into a single state for one people; not stated as a general rule.

independent-unions.rationale: One-party rule and the leader as the centre of the masses leave unions as Party transmission belts, not independent bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine claims the masses are masters of their destiny yet places power in the Party and leader, so the claim of working-class power is verbal; adherents would agree in principle.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution has the state and cooperative organisations own the means of production, so public hands for essentials is consistent.

second-chamber.rationale: The constitution sets up a single Supreme People's Assembly, so a second chamber is not part of the system.

municipal-property.rationale: The constitution recognises state and cooperative ownership, with the state dominant, so local community ownership is not its model.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Supreme leader, one-party rule and absolute central authority leave no room for local assemblies deciding things.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the state sets wages centrally and the position is inferred as neutral.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no position follows from the doctrine.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no position follows from the doctrine.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from total state control over society and the economy; untraceable money would escape it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the state's control over information and the collectivist duties in the doctrine; anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Juche in its developed form puts collectivist duties and loyalty to the leader over individual rights, treating the person as serving the collective.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is a humanist-materialist philosophy centred on man's creative autonomy, though it is secular and the state has been atheist; not directly stated.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the constitution describes a unitary state with local organs subordinate to central ones.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the self-reliance line might favour domestic agriculture but nothing is stated.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no position follows from the doctrine.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The sources stress the Korean nation and not racial groups within the country; inferred as neutral.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine stresses pride in the Korean nation, which adherents often frame by ancestry; the sources opened do not state it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The state describes its forces as defensive, yet Songun and reunification aims stand beside it; adherents' answer is inferred as neutral.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The state treats Koreans as one nation divided from outside and seeks reunification, though the sources opened do not define nation by language specifically.

communal-electorates.rationale: A single-party state with state-supervised religion would not grant communities separate electorates; inferred from the constitution's structure.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The doctrine presents US imperialism as the cause of Korea's division and as a standing threat to the DPRK.

free-public-college.rationale: The socialist state is to provide education to all; free tuition is inferred, not read in the sources opened.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Self-reliant planning and state direction of the economy point to administrative rather than price-based tools; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Juche stresses building a lasting independent country for the coming generations, but gives no environmental duty; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Women are to be liberated and mobilised as equals in the revolution rather than as bearers of distinct values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Songun and the nuclear programme put military strength first, as part of defence self-reliance.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; a closed party-state conducting diplomacy under leader guidance is unlikely to commit to open treaties; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The constitution sets a planned, state-owned economy with state control of foreign trade, implying control of cross-border capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Songun makes the army the supreme state institution and armed forces are party-controlled, so rival armed groups are not tolerated; inferred from the Songun and constitution material, which do not address private militias directly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Juche demands military self-reliance and defence of the fatherland, and the constitution makes defence a citizen duty, so refusing to fight is a betrayal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions are party-led transmission belts and wages follow the state plan, so independent collective bargaining is not part of the system; inferred from the planned economy.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The state owns production and sets wages and provides goods directly, so top-ups through tax credits do not fit; inferred from the planned economy.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: A centrally planned economy has no independent borrowing constraint and the state allocates resources by plan; inferred, as the sources do not mention fiscal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The treatise opposes imperialism and dependence on great powers and demands an independent national economy, so a fairer international order for smaller countries fits, though Juche stresses self-reliance over reform of global rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Juche began as Marxism-Leninism and defends revolutionary transformation, but it defends its own existing state; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist roots.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The constitution fixes a socialist planned economy with state and cooperative ownership, leaving no room for communities to choose other systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Pricing nature as capital is a market idea at odds with a planned economy that treats resources as state property; inferred, not stated.

sacred-nation.rationale: Juche is a nationalist doctrine that places the Korean nation and its leader at the centre of collective life and demands lifelong devotion to them.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The constitution provides free education, so student loans barely exist, and the state would favour relief; inferred from the free-education provision.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Doctrine claims the state's regions share a single collective, so exploitation of one region by another is not recognised; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The treatise says humans are social beings defined by independence, creativity and consciousness, a shared nature that grounds the masses' role, though it subordinates individual rights to the collective.

public-service-media.rationale: Media are under party control and serve to guide the masses, so independence from the government contradicts the system the sources describe.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The state is atheist in practice and Juche is a secular doctrine of human self-mastery, so a shared religious truth is not endorsed; inferred, since the constitution formally allows religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: The constitution makes land and farm cooperatives socialist property under state guidance, so state-protected farm incomes fit the system.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Military self-reliance is a pillar of Juche and Songun, and North Korea holds nuclear weapons as a deterrent, so unilateral disarmament is rejected.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Workers' Party is described as the party of the working masses, but it is the ruling party and not independent of the state, so the fit is only partial.

ban-fgm.rationale: North Korea's official line presents the system as protecting women's rights and FGM is not part of Korean custom; the sources do not discuss it, so this is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution gives women equal social status and rights with men, and the state claims to have liberated women.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Juche nationalism treats Koreans as one nation with one language and rejects the division of the peninsula; inferred, the sources do not state it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Industry is state-owned and planned, with no private-law liability as an alternative to state regulation; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Authority rests with the party and the supreme leader, so no formal role for customary chiefs exists; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The constitution commits the state to environmental protection and collective duties outrank individual rights in the doctrine; inferred for the priority claim.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The state runs a centralised legal order in which the party directs the courts, so fixed penalties are plausible; not stated in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Juche nationalism stresses Korean language and cultural purity, so requiring newcomers to learn it fits, though immigration is minimal; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unions are party-led mass organisations under the constitution, so voluntary membership is not an aim; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not discuss voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The state promotes Juche as its guiding ideology and tightly controls religion, so it would not treat all interpretations equally; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The treatise places the masses under the guidance of the party and leader, and the state is defined by that leadership, not by competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Collectivist moral duties and conservative family norms are emphasised; inferred, not stated in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The state controls information and defends its system against outside influence, which fits cutting access in a crisis; inferred and anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The state owns production and plans the economy, so welfare is provided through the plan rather than one cash payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution states that women have equal social status and rights with men.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Juche's treatment of religion is about independence and state ideology rather than women; no position is stated.

race-social-construct.rationale: Juche is strongly nationalist about the Korean nation and its purity, so adherents would not call race a mere construct; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The state organises mass women's bodies and promotes equal rights by decree; inferred from the constitution's equality clause.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The constitution makes land and key resources state or cooperative property, with no private ownership by first claim.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The treatise makes national sovereignty and independence absolute; the DPRK rejects outside judgement of its leaders.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Juche is a materialist state creed that makes man the master of his destiny, and the cult of the leader takes the place of religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: Juche is a single-nation doctrine with no Indigenous self-rule question; the DPRK proclaims sex equality but under party control.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The constitution defines the DPRK as a socialist state with a planned national economy and treats its defence as supreme.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's system of people's assemblies, where the Supreme People's Assembly elects top state bodies.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: the state privileges no church, and religion is formally allowed but strictly controlled, with Juche itself dominant.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK presents itself as a single homogeneous nation and has no ethnic autonomy regions.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK holds that Korean reunification is for the nation and its leadership to settle, not by local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Juche is a Korean nationalism of one divided nation and regards the division of Korea as an imposed foreign line to be undone.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the self-reliance principle and the call for hard struggle, though the state also promises abundance.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the question of an indigenous majority does not arise in a doctrine of one homogeneous nation.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the DPRK conscripts both sexes for long service and the doctrine of total mobilisation does not distinguish them, though sources do not discuss it.

missingStatements.text: The national leader should hold supreme, lifelong authority as the centre around which the party and masses are united.
missingStatements.rationale: The suryong theory casts the leader as the centre of the masses and absolute supreme leader, central to Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism.

missingStatements.text: A country's armed forces should come first in state policy, ahead of other sectors.
missingStatements.rationale: Songun (military-first politics) made the National Defence Commission the supreme state body in the 1998 revision and is written into the constitution.

missingStatements.text: A country should build a self-reliant economy based on its own heavy industry rather than depend on foreign supply.
missingStatements.rationale: The treatise and the constitution make an independent national economy built on heavy industry a pillar of sovereignty.

notes: Many answers are inferred because the doctrine addresses few domestic social issues directly; the sources describe stated principles, not North Korean practice. Kim Jong Un-era changes (people-first politics, hostile-state doctrine toward South Korea, removal of reunification) shift some answers, such as reunification.
